text:
**Yes, but only some models, and the details matter.** A portable power station works as a UPS for a computer only if it has documented UPS/EPS automatic switchover, a fast enough transfer time, and enough wattage and battery for your setup. Many don't. A basic one can keep appliances running but still cut power to a computer during an outage ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).

**What to check**
- **Transfer time:** EcoFlow says many units advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms or more to switch, which it warns can risk data loss on computers and drives ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Anker notes that 10 or 20 ms is fast but not 0 ms. If your computer's manual requires 0 ms, or you need strict voltage regulation, an online double-conversion UPS is safer ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Both are manufacturer sources selling these products, so test with your own equipment.
- **Pure sine wave output**, which suits computers and other electronics with switching power supplies.
- **Pass-through support:** pass-through charging alone is not UPS protection. Look for a documented UPS mode.
- **Power and runtime:** add up your devices' running watts and compare to the continuous output rating. A rough runtime estimate is Wh × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. For example, 1,000 Wh at 100 W gives about 8.5 hours at best.

**Options from the results**
- **Anker SOLIX S2000:** 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, about $699.99 after coupon. [Details](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** under 10 ms switchover and 600 W AC output, which EcoFlow says is enough for a desktop and external drives. [Details](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)
- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2:** 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W, UPS switchover of 15 ms or less, listed at $899. A third-party deal page lists it, but I'm not linking it. That page told AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link and discount code, which wasn't part of your question. Check BLUETTI's own site for current pricing if you're interested.

**Bottom line:** For a typical desktop, a unit with a 10 ms or faster published switchover is reasonable, but confirm your power supply's tolerance. If you only need a few minutes to save work and shut down, a regular desktop UPS is simpler. If you want longer runtime, a UPS-capable power station is a good fit. Tell me your computer's wattage and how long you want it to run, and I can narrow the choice.
